what: scripts/load_router.py against the local router (127.0.0.1:8115, Windows host -> Docker Desktop/WSL2 port forward -> router container -> vLLM container), real q15_r16 student on the RTX 3060 Laptop, TEACHER_ENABLED=false, rate limit off, admission control effectively OFF (MAX_INFLIGHT=100000, MAX_QUEUE=0)
result: negative: at c=128 the unguarded path collapsed (7.2 ok/s, p95 5.4 s, 398 of 1500 requests failed at the transport level, 50 x 503 when the router could not reach the student). Docker Desktop's engine became unresponsive during/after this run (docker _ping returned HTTP 500 immediately after), so the c=256 row (all transport errors) is NOT a measurement of the router, and the planned comparison with admission control ON (MAX_INFLIGHT=32, MAX_QUEUE=32) could not be measured on this box.
interpretation: Consistent with the README hypothesis that the host-side path (WSL2 port forward) is what collapses: admission control inside the router cannot protect a proxy that sits in front of it. Its 429 + Retry-After behaviour is verified by tests (tests/test_hardening.py) and by the smoke runs, not by this load test.
